result.title: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Workshop BeNTo: Beyond Next Token Prediction
result.summary: Discrete graph diffusion models (GDMs) corrupt the graph structure by adding noise independently to nodes and edges under a Markovian noise model. In the unconditional setting without node features, an equivariant denoiser trained on a single graph is able to generate novel graphs and sample-level metrics such as edge overlap and WL kernel similarity find no evidence of memorization. In this work, we challenge this view and show for the first time that graph diffusion models indeed exhibit memorization. Analyzing the reverse diffusion trajectories of GDMs trained on two-block stochastic block models (SBMs), we find a strong train-data bias: the model recovers a corrupted training graph almost perfectly compared to a held-out test graph. We term this conditional memorization, as it surfaces only when the reverse trajectory is conditioned on a corrupted training graph and is not apparent during inference. It coincides with a growing generalization gap, where the training loss improves as the loss on held-out graphs degrades, and it cannot be mitigated by early stopping. The onset of memorization always precedes the emergence of community structure in the generated graphs, thus every checkpoint earlier produces structureless graphs. This behavior holds across all node sizes we test.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究离散图扩散模型的记忆现象：在双块 SBM 上分析反向扩散轨迹，发现模型对以被破坏训练图为条件的轨迹几乎完美恢复训练图（称为「条件记忆」），该现象在常规采样指标下不可见，并与泛化差距扩大同时出现，早停无法缓解，且总是先于社区结构生成出现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以损坏训练输入为条件、观察反向轨迹能否完美还原」的轨迹级诊断，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正使用了视觉证据、而非记忆训练分布捷径提供可借鉴的对照思路，但属推测性迁移。
